articles.title: The Interview - Peter Obi, Nigerian presidential candidate: The last election was rigged - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Nigerian opposition leader Peter Obi on his presidential bid and his claim he won in 2023
articles.body:
World Service , · 16 Oct 2026 , · 23 mins

“Nigeria can fight insecurity, head on. It only requires it for the commander-in-chief to be determined that this will end. Those criminals live with us. In our communities, people know them. I will go to the communities and find them. I will take control. And I will not do it from Abuja.” Madina Maishanu speaks to Peter Obi, one of Nigeria’s leading opposition politicians, now with the Nigeria Democratic Congress, and a former governor of Anambra State. He came third in the 2023 presidential election, attracting significant support from young Nigerians fed up with unemployment and police brutality who demanded political change. But Obi has never accepted the outcome, insisting he won and that the official results were manipulated, although Nigeria's courts rejected his challenge. Now he's hoping to become president in 2027, promising to address some of Nigeria's biggest problems, including widespread insecurity and government corruption. The Interview brings you the best interviews coming from the BBC, including episodes with the head of the World Meteorological Organisation, Celeste Saulo and the former Australian prime minister Julia Gillard. You can listen on the BBC World Service on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays at 0800 GMT. Or you can listen to The Interview as a podcast, out three times a week on BBC Sounds or wherever you get your podcasts. articles.title: Why is Alberta voting to separate from Canada, and how likely is it to happen?
articles.summary: The oil-rich province will decide on Monday whether to stay part of Canada or trigger a binding independence referendum.
articles.body:
The western Canadian province of Alberta will ask its citizens on Monday whether they want to remain part of Canada or kick-start the process of holding a binding referendum on separation.

The vote will mark a major test of the country's unity, the first in decades.

Alberta's leader, Premier Danielle Smith, announced in May that the question on independence would be put to voters, though she herself supports a unified Canada.

There has been a growing separatist sentiment in the oil-rich province in recent years, and the vote comes after 300,000 people signed a petition asking that a referendum be held on the matter.

Here's why some Albertans are calling for independence and what comes next.

The question being put to voters won't be a simple "stay" or "leave".

Instead, Albertans will be asked: "Should Alberta remain a province of Canada or should the Government of Alberta commence the legal process required under the Canadian Constitution to hold a binding provincial referendum on whether or not Alberta should separate from Canada?"

The premier's office clarified to the BBC that voters will have a choice of checking two boxes - option A being to remain in Canada and option B being to start the legal process to hold a binding separation referendum.

There are 10 questions. What about the others?

There are nine other questions that have been put to voters, though they have been overshadowed by the one on independence.

They deal with two main topics: immigration and Constitutional matters.

For the most part, all of them seek to ask Albertans about options to gain more autonomy from Ottawa.

On immigration, voters will be asked whether they want the province to have increased control over immigration, to bring it to "more sustainable levels" and introducing a law requiring people to provide proof of citizenship to vote in an Alberta provincial election.

The rest focus on access to social services like healthcare for non-permanent residents.

The Constitutional questions include one seeking to allow provinces to push for the power to elect provincial judges and for an elected Senate. Senators in Canada are currently appointed by the governor general on the advice of the prime minister.

'We have more in common with America than the rest of Canada'

How oil-rich Alberta's economy might fare if it broke away from Canada

Canada PM warns 'stakes are high' as Alberta separation vote nears

The referendum question is a result of a push by a group of Albertans who have been advocating for the province to be independent from Canada.

Over the past year, they held townhalls across the province to gauge interest from the public. They then launched a citizen-led petition to separate earlier this year, which gathered more than 300,000 signatures.

But the petition was blocked by an Alberta court early this year.

A judge ruled that Alberta, which authorised the gathering of signatures for a proposed independence referendum under a citizen petition law, failed to consult indigenous First Nations whose land would be affected should the province become an independent state.

Meanwhile, another group led by a former deputy premier of Alberta, Thomas Lukaszuk, collected signatures for an anti-separation petition called Forever Canadian. That was signed by more than 400,000 Albertans.

The province's population is slightly more than five million.

Smith said in May that she was "deeply troubled" by the court decision, and will not let "a single judge silence the voices of hundreds of thousands of Albertans".

Her government has appealed against the decision, she said. But in the meantime, "kicking the can down the road only prolongs a very emotional and important debate".

She has also faced pressure from separatist Albertans, some within her own political party, to hold a referendum on independence regardless of the legal decision.

At Canada's biggest rodeo, the starting gun is fired in the fight over Alberta separation

Who are the separatists, and what do they want?

The separatist movement is led by Mitch Sylvestre, a gun shop owner from the town of Bonnyville, and Jeffrey Rath, a lawyer based in Calgary. It has been supported by other figures along the way.

Both Sylvestre and Rath are members of a group called the Alberta Prosperity Project, which argues that the province's economic growth has been hindered by years of Liberal party rule in Ottawa.

In particular, many in the movement are frustrated with environmental policies that they believe have stood in the way of building pipelines and unlocking resources from the oil-rich province, which traditionally leans conservative.

They also believe that Alberta contributes far more to the country than it receives, and that Ottawa has a disproportionate say in its internal matters.

The sentiment is rooted in "western alienation" - a term that has been used for decades to describe the sense by some in Canada's western provinces that they are often overlooked and underrepresented by federal politicians in Canada's capital.

But the movement is not uniform in its demands.

At a separatist townhall last year, some told the BBC that they wanted to use the threat of independence as a bargaining chip with Ottawa, while others said they would like to follow through with a provincial divorce.

A few said they would be open to Alberta joining the US.

Rath has told the BBC that he believes Alberta has more in common culturally with parts of the US than the rest of Canada.

He has also travelled to Washington several times on what he has described as a "fact-finding" mission, where he and other separatists met Trump administration officials to see if the US government would support an independent Alberta with a line of credit.

Rath has not publicly named which Trump officials the group has met.

Alberta Elections have their work cut out for them.

All the ballots - a separate colour-coded one for each question - will be counted by hand.

They have 48 hours to complete the count, which starts at 20:00 local time on Monday (03:00 BST Tuesday) and can be delayed if there are voters still in line.

Question 10, on separation, will be counted in its entirety first, given the high interest in that result.

Alberta Elections said that results for that question should be available in the early hours of Tuesday.

The launch of a referendum triggered a five-month campaign period for interested parties on both sides of the issue.

Smith said she will vote for Albert to remain. She argues that, while some grievances raised by the separatists are legitimate, the province has recently been able to make significant inroads with Ottawa, including on developing a pipeline project.

Prime Minister Mark Carney, who has ambitions of making Canada an "energy superpower", has pressed the case for the province to stay.

"We're renovating the country as we go, and Alberta being at the centre of that is essential," Carney, who was raised in Edmonton, Alberta, said in May.

Opposition Conservative leader Pierre Poilievre, who enjoys significant support in Alberta and who was raised in Calgary, also said that his party will be advocating for unity.

Meanwhile, Rath, one of the most prominent separatist voices, has expressed disappointment in the referendum question put forward by Smith, arguing it should have been a direct "stay or leave" option.

He has threatened to organise a vote against her leadership of Alberta's United Conservative Party, which could put Smith's political future in jeopardy.

"To hell with 301,620 Albertans who were promised a vote on their question," he wrote on social media following her announcement. "Danielle Smith just lost her base!"

First Nations in Alberta have also criticised Smith, calling her decision to hold a referendum despite the court ruling "undemocratic" and "authoritarian".

If Albertans vote to leave, Smith said that would kickstart a "legal process" to hold a binding referendum, adding there are a number of steps that would have to be taken to get there.

"I will accept the result of this referendum," she said. "That's why I'll be campaigning hard to try to convince Albertans of my position, which is to remain."

She has since said if Albertans vote to move ahead with a binding referendum, that could happen as soon as 2027.

How many Albertans support independence?

Polls suggest that the majority of Albertans would vote to remain in Canada.

A Leger poll published earlier this month suggests that 70% of Albertans want the province to stay as it is.

Just over 20% would vote to begin the legal process for a future binding referendum on separation. And 7% of respondents were undecided.

A September poll by Janet Brown Opinion Research for broadcaster CBC suggested 72% support for the remain side, and 23% for the leave side, with slightly higher support among male and rural voters.

Despite the lack of popular support, there are concerns of a Brexit-style upset, when UK voters surprised pollsters by voting to leave the European Union, especially if people choose to 'send a message' to Ottawa.

However, that scenario is seen as unlikely.

articles.title: A rare family of barn owls moved into Manhattan's Upper West Side. New Yorkers are captivated
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Manhattan's Upper West Side has been reveling in the company of its latest celebrities: A family of barn owls nested in a water tower atop a...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Manhattan's Upper West Side has been reveling in the company of its latest celebrities: A family of barn owls nested in a water tower atop a building near Central Park.

This is the first documented instance of barn owls nesting in Manhattan in modern history, according to one expert, and the owls have attracted nightly crowds of people in the street eager to get a glimpse of the elusive birds.

"It was, like, totally shocking," Andrew Farnsworth, a migration ecologist at the Cornell Lab of Ornithology, said of the barn owls. "To the best of our knowledge, like the collective birding knowledge, there hasn't been a nest in, you know, in Manhattan, at least in recorded history."

Word of the barn owl family didn't get around until last week, when Elisabeth Williams, an Upper West Side resident, notified a local news outlet on Oct. 6 that she and her husband saw multiple owls at the water tower atop a building on West 75th Street close to Central Park West.

The couple had previously seen a single owl on an apartment windowsill a few days earlier and were shocked even then, Williams recalled.

"In a place like Manhattan, you normally really have to go out of your way to encounter nature," she said. "And here it was, just sort of right outside our window."

Barn owl sightings are rare in New York City

It's not the first time that birds have captivated New Yorkers. Residents have fallen in love with American woodcocks , who are known to stop in Midtown Manhattan's Bryant Park every year as they migrate north in early spring. After Flaco the Eurasian eagle-owl died in 2024 , dozens of mournful fans gathered to say goodbye to the beloved creature who flew around Manhattan and became a joy to many after someone let him out of his zoo enclosure the previous year. Then there was Pale Male, a red-tailed hawk who nested above Fifth Avenue for three decades before dying in 2023.

But barn owl sightings in New York City parks are very rare, according to the New York City Department of Parks & Recreation. New York is at the northern fringe of the barn owl's range and the barn owl population has declined "at an alarming rate" over time, according to the state Department of Environmental Conservation.

"There's lots of excitement among New Yorkers, both birders and non-birders alike, about these owls because owls really capture the attention," said Jessica Wilson, executive director of NYC Bird Alliance. "They're magical, they're nocturnal, they are secretive, they're not commonly seen, especially on the Upper West Side of Manhattan. And to have this chance to see these birds is really thrilling."

Photographers and casual onlookers have gathered on the street on a nightly basis to spot the owls.

"I've only seen one barn owl ever, and that was in California," said Val Coleman, a retired New York City resident who was on the Upper West Side earlier this week trying to spot the owls. "At dusk, we hope they will come out to hunt. We hope they don't eat poisoned rats with rodenticide in 'em."

David Barrett, a Manhattan-based birder who runs the popular social media account, Manhattan Bird Alert, said he's observed at least one adult barn owl and five fledglings at the water tower. He's also seen an adult owl carrying rodents back to the water tower. There are believed to be two adult owls, and some photographers have claimed to have seen six fledglings, Barrett added.

"Having one barn owl is a rarity, but it's not national news. Having a family, for the first time ever, breeding in Manhattan in recorded history, that's special news," Barrett said.

Before the recent barn owl sightings, Williams and her husband heard periodic screeching noises outside going back to early September. They initially assumed it was a bird of some kind but were skeptical when a phone app indicated the noise was from a barn owl.

Thomas Obersteiner said that he first heard bizarre screeching and wailing noises from outside one evening in mid-September. It sounded like someone was "being murdered outside," he said.

"That lasted for two or three weeks, every night, sometimes more, sometimes less, coming from different directions," Obersteiner added. "But I had no idea what that was."

On multiple occasions, Obersteiner or his wife ran into their children's bedroom after mistaking the owls' screech for a child in pain, he said. It wasn't until he saw a news report that he realized that owls were making the sounds.

Farnsworth said the screech is typical of barn owls, who use it to communicate with one another. The screech is like a "horror movie kind of experience," he said.

Obersteiner, who said his roof deck is "probably the best location in town right now" to watch the owls, has been letting nature photographers access that perch to observe the owls "almost every night" since news of the barn owls spread. On one night last week, 20 people had gathered.

"We can't say no because it's so much fun and these people are so serious," Obersteiner added. "It's beautiful."

Williams and her husband were not bird watchers before the barn owl family moved in to the water tower. But that may change soon after their "delightful" experience.

"I think we're about to become birders," Williams said.

articles.title: Nova chefe de imprensa de Trump admite que reprovou no exame de advocacia | G1
articles.standfirst: Katie Zacharia foi apresentada por Donald Trump como advogada e disse diversas vezes que é jurista. Nova porta-voz estreou no cargo nesta semana e substitui Karoline Leavitt, que deixou o posto para se dedicar à família.
articles.summary: Katie Zacharia foi apresentada por Donald Trump como advogada e disse diversas vezes que é jurista. Nova porta-voz estreou no cargo nesta semana e substitui Karoline Leavitt, que deixou o posto para se dedicar à família.
articles.body:
A nova secretária de imprensa da Casa Branca, Katie Zacharia, admitiu na quinta-feira (15) que não foi aprovada no exame para exercer a advocacia nos Estados Unidos, ao contrário do que havia afirmado .

Menos de uma semana após assumir o cargo, Zacharia, de 41 anos, levantou dúvidas sobre suas credenciais ao se apresentar, nas redes sociais e em programas de televisão, como assessora jurídica .

Ela disse prestava assessoria para uma organização conservadora sem fins lucrativos sediada na Califórnia e que havia trabalhado como advogada em um escritório em Pequim .

No entanto, as credenciais jurídicas de Zacharia foram postas em xeque depois que ela deu uma resposta vaga sobre onde havia sido aprovada no exame da ordem.

👉 Zacharia formou-se em Direito pela Universidade Pepperdine em 2011, mas obter o diploma não habilita automaticamente alguém a exercer a profissão. Em uma entrevista à Fox News na quinta-feira, o apresentador Sean Hannity perguntou-lhe: "A senhora fez o exame da ordem, mas não foi aprovada, correto?" .

Nova porta-voz do governo Trump, Katie Zacharia, faz sua primeira entrevista coletiva na Casa Branca, em Washington, D.C., nos Estados Unidos, em 13 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Kevin Lamarque

Em uma entrevista anterior ao veículo conservador Real America's Voice, Zacharia gerou dúvidas sobre a veracidade de suas credenciais. Na entrevista, ela disse que se inscreveu para fazer o exame, mas estava "distraída e sobrecarregada" com os planos de mudança para a China com o marido.

"Os resultados são, de certa forma, irrelevantes, porque eu sabia que não precisaria do título de advogada na China", disse ela. No entanto, cidadãos estrangeiros não podem prestar o exame da ordem na China, embora possam realizar certos trabalhos jurídicos em escritórios de advocacia chineses.

Na entrevista com Hannity, foi questionada se havia feito o exame uma segunda vez, ao que ela respondeu: "Não fiz". "Tive quatro filhos em seis anos", disse ela. "Nunca foi minha intenção exercer a advocacia".

Zacharia disse na Real America's Voice que "muitas pessoas do setor" haviam lhe garantido que ela poderia atuar como advogada, dado o seu diploma em direito e a experiência em direito empresarial que obteve na China.

Ela acrescentou que poderia "oferecer análises jurídicas, não consultoria jurídica".

A organização de ética política Campaign for Accountability solicitou, na quarta-feira, que a Ordem dos Advogados da Califórnia iniciasse uma investigação.

"Na Califórnia, intitular-se advogado sem licença não é um exagero; é crime", afirmou a organização em um comunicado à imprensa.

Zacharia conduziu sua breve primeira coletiva de imprensa na terça-feira e respondeu apenas a perguntas de três jornalistas.

A republicana substitui Karoline Leavitt, uma aliada convicta do presidente Donald Trump que liderou uma estratégia de comunicação agressiva contra a mídia tradicional antes de renunciar, em agosto, para dedicar mais tempo à família.

articles.title: Fervedouro Rio Azul: como chegar em nascente de águas cristalinas   | G1
articles.standfirst: Após as chuvas intensas, nível do Rio Azul subiu cerca de 10 metros e cobriu áreas antes secas. O g1 foi até o local e registrou o cenário que encanta turistas.
articles.summary: Após as chuvas intensas, nível do Rio Azul subiu cerca de 10 metros e cobriu áreas antes secas, criando um cenário de águas azuladas em meio à vegetação da Serra da Bodoquena.
articles.body:
As chuvas intensas dos últimos dias na Serra da Bodoquena , em Mato Grosso do Sul, transformaram a paisagem do Rio Azul, um dos atrativos naturais de Bodoquena. Com o nível da água cerca de 10 metros acima do normal, áreas que antes ficavam em terra firme foram inundadas.

A chuva também transformou um dos cenários mais fascinantes da região: o Fervedouro Rio Azul. A cheia revelou um cenário submerso de tirar o fôlego que tem encantado turistas e também seguidores nas redes sociais.

A reportagem do g1 foi até o local e desbravou o cenário de águas azuladas em contraste com a vegetação verde.

🔎 Fervedouro é uma nascente de água subterrânea em que a pressão da água faz com que ela brote continuamente do solo.

📍 Como chegar: o atrativo fica a 19,5 km do centro Bodoquena e a visitação funciona obrigatoriamente por meio de agências de turismo credenciadas no município. Cada empresa organiza os horários, valores e as datas disponíveis para os passeios.

A mudança na paisagem surpreendeu turistas de Minas Gerais, Santa Catarina e do interior de São Paulo, que visitaram o atrativo para conhecer de perto as águas cristalinas e a diversidade de peixes.

A funcionária pública Luciana Borges contou que estava ansiosa para observar os peixes pessoalmente, depois de conhecer o local por meio de vídeos.

“Tem muito peixe, pelo menos é o que a gente vê nos vídeos, então quero ver pessoalmente!”, disse.

Depois de receberem as orientações dos guias, os visitantes seguiram de barco e percorreram uma trilha até uma das nascentes do Rio Azul.

No local, encontraram uma paisagem modificada pela elevação do nível da água, que chegou a cobrir estruturas instaladas às margens do rio, como um banco que normalmente fica fora da água.

Apesar da mudança, a transparência da água continuou revelando os tons azulados do rio, que contrastam com o verde intenso da vegetação.

Para a publicitária Jéssica Cristina Lemes da Silva, a combinação de cores torna o cenário especial.

“Nunca me acostumo com a beleza. Eu acho que o tom da água, com a vegetação, o contraste, acho lindíssimo”, afirmou.

Fervedouro Rio Azul em Bodoquena (MS) — Foto: Jean Kelvin

Entenda por que o nível do Rio Azul subiu

De acordo com o guia turístico Carlos Henrique de Oliveira Ferreira, a elevação do nível do Rio Azul está relacionada à influência do Rio Salobra, o maior da região de Bodoquena. Com as chuvas, o aumento do volume de água do Salobra provoca o represamento do Rio Azul.

Segundo o guia, enquanto as águas do Salobra chegam com aspecto mais turvo, as nascentes do Rio Azul mantêm a transparência característica do atrativo. A diferença entre as águas pode ser observada no encontro dos dois rios.

“A água do Rio Salobra que represa, ela vem turva, um pouquinho mais suja. Mas a nascente do Rio Azul, como é uma água limpa, cristalina e menos densa, ela acaba empurrando a água turva para fora e o visitante aproveita 100% da flutuação”, explicou.

O passeio também inclui a visita a um fervedouro, uma nascente em que a pressão da água provoca a movimentação dos sedimentos no fundo do rio, criando um efeito de borbulhamento.

A experiência chamou a atenção da turismóloga Vitória de Carvalho Cardoso dos Santos, que descreveu a sensação de estar no local como uma conexão especial com o ambiente natural.

“É mágico, parece que a natureza está conversando comigo. Eu falo que esse contato com a natureza é uma coisa surreal”, contou.

Entre os visitantes estava Shannon Egan, turista norte-americana que mora em Belo Horizonte, em Minas Gerais. Para ela, a experiência de observar os fenômenos naturais e entrar em contato com a água cristalina tornou o passeio inesquecível.

“É uma experiência única, para afundar e ver todas as coisas acontecendo, para conectar com a natureza. Esse jeitinho! É muito legal!”, relatou.

articles.title: Arquiteto de 59 anos morre após infarto em Goiânia | G1
articles.standfirst: Getúlio Lima Júnior, de 59 anos, morava sozinho e chegou a ligar para a emergência, segundo amiga da família. Velório e sepultamento serão realizados na tarde desta sexta-feira (16), em Itumbiara.
articles.summary: Getúlio Lima Júnior morava sozinho em Goiânia e chegou a acionar a emergência, segundo amiga da família. Ele será velado e sepultado nesta sexta-feira, em Itumbiara.
articles.body:
O arquiteto Getúlio Lima Júnior, de 59 anos, morreu após sofrer um infarto em Goiânia , segundo a família. Ele estava sozinho no apartamento e chegou a acionar a emergência, mas morreu antes da chegada da equipe, contou uma amiga da família ao g1 .

Natural de Itumbiara , no sul de Goiás, Getúlio era filho de Getúlio Lima e Edma Honorina de Carvalho Lima, ambos já falecidos e conhecidos na cidade.

Segundo a prima dele, a arquiteta Daniella Lima, Getúlio deixou um filho, que estuda Medicina, e mantinha vínculos familiares e amizades em sua cidade natal.

Getúlio Junior morreu em casa de infarto — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais de Getúlio Lima

De acordo com Daniella, o velório e o sepultamento serão realizados na tarde desta sexta-feira (16), em Itumbiara. A cerimônia de despedida está prevista para começar às 13h30, na Funerária Fênix. O sepultamento deve ocorrer às 15h30, no Cemitério Avenida da Saudade, conhecido como Cemitério Velho.

Nas redes sociais, amigos e familiares lamentaram a morte do arquiteto Getúlio Lima Júnior. A irmã dele, Claudia Zuppani, disse que estava longe, mas tentaria voltar a tempo de se despedir do irmão.

“Dia de luto e tristeza. Perdi meu irmão. Eu longe, tentando voltar pra casa pra me despedir dele. Orem por nós”, escreveu.

A prima Marina Zuppani também publicou uma homenagem ao arquiteto. “Meu amado primo! Ser humano maravilhoso”, escreveu.

Karine Campos, também prima de Getúlio, relembrou o último encontro entre os dois e lamentou a despedida. Segundo ela, os familiares tinham planos de se encontrar novamente.

“Meu coração sente tristeza e dor. A vida é um sopro. Dia 24/09 nosso reencontro e foi muito bom, tínhamos mais planos de encontros e hoje sua despedida de nós. Meu primo partiu para junto do Pai. Descanse em paz, ficará para sempre no meu coração e minhas lembranças, meu primo querido”, escreveu.

articles.title: Lojas viraram vitrines da internet? Entenda como os brasileiros estão mudando a forma de comprar | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento revela que consumidores transitam cada vez mais entre lojas físicas e digitais. Preço, promoções e disponibilidade dos produtos influenciam a decisão de compra e desafiam o comércio tradicional.
articles.summary: Pesquisa mostra que 76% dos consumidores já viram um produto na loja e compraram pela internet; especialista aponta que a integração entre os canais é um desafio para o varejo.
articles.body:
Segundo a primeira edição do Radar Smollan, realizada em agosto deste ano, 76% dos entrevistados afirmaram já ter visto um produto em uma loja física e comprado pela internet posteriormente — Foto: Divulgação

Como mostrou o g1 em agosto, o comércio varejista tem enfrentado dificuldades para fechar as contas. Reduzir o número de lojas, cortar custos e investir em operações mais eficientes se tornaram parte das estratégias para reverter os números ruins.

Outro motivo para essa revisão das operações é a mudança no comportamento do consumidor . Ele pesquisa preços na internet, visita lojas para conhecer os produtos e, muitas vezes, finaliza a compra no comércio eletrônico.

Esse comportamento, conhecido como "showrooming", ajuda a ilustrar um dos desafios do varejo tradicional:

🤔 Como manter a relevância das lojas físicas em um mercado no qual os consumidores comparam preços com facilidade e têm cada vez mais opções on-line?

Enquanto marketplaces e plataformas digitais ampliam a concorrência e pressionam os preços, o comprador enfrenta um aperto financeiro com os juros elevados e crédito caro, que limitam o espaço das famílias para consumir.

Nesse cenário, a loja física está perdendo espaço para o comércio eletrônico ou ganhando um novo papel na jornada de compra?

Uma pesquisa da Smollan, empresa de soluções para o varejo, mostra como a jornada de compra já combina os ambientes físico e digital.

Segundo pesquisa da empresa, realizada em agosto deste ano, 76% dos entrevistados afirmaram já ter visto um produto em uma loja física e comprado pela internet posteriormente.

O movimento também ocorre no sentido inverso:

81% disseram pesquisar na internet antes de realizar uma compra em uma loja física;

87% afirmaram já ter entrado em uma loja para comprar um produto e saído com outro.

O levantamento reuniu 1.828 conversas com consumidores de 156 cidades, distribuídas por 25 estados.

"O digital mudou a forma como o consumidor chega à loja, mas não reduziu a capacidade do ponto de venda de influenciar a escolha", afirma Renato Vechiatto, diretor de operações (COO) da Smollan para a América Latina.

“O consumidor chega à loja mais informado e, muitas vezes, já tem uma decisão encaminhada. Ainda assim, fatores como preço, disponibilidade, promoções e experiência de compra podem influenciar sua escolha. Para as marcas, isso reforça a importância de garantir que os produtos estejam disponíveis e bem apresentados nas lojas”, afirma Vechiatto.

Por que o consumidor ainda vai à loja física?

Mesmo com a facilidade de pesquisar preços e comprar pela internet, ver o produto pessoalmente continua sendo um dos motivos para visitar uma loja.

Na pesquisa, 46,1% dos entrevistados apontaram essa experiência como um fator importante para ir ao ponto de venda. Outros 29,2% destacaram a vantagem de sair da loja com o produto em mãos.

🥘 A preferência pelo canal varia conforme a categoria:

Para comprar carne, 93,4% dos consumidores preferem lojas físicas;

No caso de hortifrútis, o percentual chega a 92% .

📱 Já no segmento de eletrônicos, as preferências são mais divididas:

A diferença mostra que a experiência presencial continua relevante, mas seu peso depende do produto e das necessidades do consumidor.

Em alguns casos, tocar, experimentar ou avaliar pessoalmente um item ajuda a reduzir a insegurança antes da compra. Em outros, a praticidade e a possibilidade de comparar preços on-line podem ser determinantes.

Para Vechiatto, os canais não precisam competir entre si. O varejista pode usar a loja para oferecer uma experiência que o ambiente digital não proporciona da mesma forma e, quando não consegue igualar o preço on-line, apresentar alternativas para concretizar a venda.

“Nem sempre será possível cobrir o preço do comércio eletrônico, mas é possível oferecer outras alternativas, como crediário, seguro e acessórios, ou até apresentar outro modelo de produto. A capacitação dos vendedores é importante para que a experiência seja única", afirma Vechiatto.

O executivo também destaca que a comparação de preços é mais simples no comércio eletrônico, enquanto a loja física oferece a possibilidade de conhecer o produto pessoalmente.

Nesse caso, o atendimento e a segurança durante a compra podem ajudar a convencer o consumidor a concluir a transação presencialmente.

Preço e disponibilidade podem mudar a decisão

Compras em sites brasileiros que não informam produtos vindos da China frustram consumidores e-commerce comércio on-line compras internacionais cartão de crédito consumo — Foto: Thaisa Figueiredo/g1

A disputa entre os canais também passa pela capacidade de oferecer o produto certo, pelo preço esperado e no momento em que o consumidor deseja comprá-lo.

Na pesquisa, o preço foi apontado como fator importante na decisão de compra por 77,7% dos entrevistados.

As promoções apareceram em seguida, citadas por 61,1% . Marca (41,1%) , disponibilidade do produto (23,2%) e atendimento (20,6%) também foram mencionados.

Quando questionados sobre o que mais chama a atenção dentro da loja, 59,6% destacaram as ofertas promocionais .

O levantamento também identificou um problema que pode levar à perda de vendas: 27% dos entrevistados disseram que a disponibilidade dos produtos é o aspecto que mais precisa melhorar nas lojas, à frente dos preços (20,9%) e da integração entre os canais físico e on-line (17,6%).

Além disso, 57% afirmaram já ter desistido de uma compra em uma loja física por não encontrar o produto que procuravam.

“A falta de um produto pode levar o consumidor a desistir não apenas daquele item, mas também de continuar comprando na loja. Por isso, garantir a disponibilidade e a boa exposição dos produtos no ponto de venda é tão importante para os resultados das marcas”, afirma Vechiatto.

A falta de integração entre os canais pode agravar o problema. Se o consumidor encontra um produto na internet, mas não consegue localizá-lo na loja ou não tem acesso a informações claras sobre estoque e entrega, a empresa corre o risco de perder a venda para um concorrente.

Por isso, manter estoques adequados e integrar as informações entre lojas, centros de distribuição e plataformas digitais se torna importante para evitar que o consumidor encontre o produto em um canal, mas não consiga comprá-lo nas condições desejadas.

Black Friday no Amapá — Foto: Mariana Ferreira/g1

Como o g1 mostrou, as mudanças no comportamento do consumidor têm pressionado varejistas e redes de lojas físicas a rever suas operações . Manter esses estabelecimentos envolve custos com aluguel, funcionários, estoque e logística, o que leva as empresas a priorizar unidades mais rentáveis e formatos menores.

No varejo alimentar, juros elevados, crédito caro e consumidores mais atentos aos preços reforçam a busca por eficiência e integração com os canais digitais. Isso não significa o fim das lojas físicas, mas uma mudança em seu papel na jornada de compra, segundo Renato Vechiatto.

“A gente prevê um alinhamento, uma linguagem única, mantendo as características de cada canal. O consumidor que busca essencialmente preço pode ir até a loja física, mas ser orientado a comprar no digital. Os canais sempre serão ambientes que se complementam, mas a integração permite que o varejista não perca vendas para a concorrência.”

Segundo o diretor de operações da Smollan, essa integração também passa por mudanças na logística, como parcerias entre varejistas e centros de distribuição que reduzam custos e agilizem entregas.

Há também formatos que exigem estruturas menores, como lojas de automóveis com poucos veículos em exposição e operações de delivery e dark kitchens, voltadas exclusivamente à preparação de pedidos para entrega.

O showrooming, portanto, não representa necessariamente o fim das lojas físicas, mas reforça a necessidade de oferecer preços competitivos, disponibilidade e uma boa experiência, independentemente do canal de compra.

articles.title: VÍDEO: Carros são arrastados pela chuva na Zona Sul de SP, durante temporal da madrugada desta sexta-feira | G1
articles.standfirst: Chuva que caiu na madrugada começou por volta das 01h47 da manhã e deixou todas as regiões da cidade em estado de atenção para alagamentos, segundo o CGE. Registro dos carros amontoados foi feito na Rua Horácio Alves da Costa, região da Av. Cupecê.
articles.summary: Chuva que caiu na madrugada começou por volta das 01h47 da manhã e deixou todas as regiões da cidade em estado de atenção para alagamentos, segundo o CGE.
articles.body:
Pelo menos 29 carros foram arrastados por uma enchente causada pela chuva forte que caiu na cidade de São Paulo na madrugada desta sexta-feira (16). É o segundo grande temporal que atinge a capital paulista nesta semana (veja mais abaixo).

O registro dos carros amontoados foi feito nas imediações da Avenida Cupecê, na Rua Horácio Alves da Costa, Zona Sul de São Paulo, pelo Globocop, da Tv Globo, durante a exibição no Bom Dia SP . O local fical no limite entre a capital e a cidade de Diadema .

Imagens enviadas por moradores da região da Praça Luigi Palma também mostraram a situação das ruas da Zona Sul de durante a madrugada.

Carros são arrastados por enchente na Zona Sul de São Paulo na madrugada desta sexta-feira (16). — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Por volta das 08h30, o Globocop também flagrou retroescavadeiras e caminhões da Prefeitura de Diadema fazendo a limpeza de vias no interno do terminal de ônibus central da cidade, em razão da sujeito e do barro causado pelos alagamentos da madrugada.

A chuva começou por volta das 01h47 da manhã e deixou todas as regiões da cidade em estado de atenção para alagamentos, segundo o Centro de Controle de Emergências Climáticas (CGE), da Prefeitura de São Paulo.

O término do estado de atenção terminou apenas por volta das 05h13 da manhã.

Limpeza das ruas de Diadema em razão do temporal que caiu na madrugada desta sexta-feira (16). — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Segundo o CGE, os maiores índices acumulados de chuva nas estações meteorológicas automáticas do CGE nesta sexta (16) foram nas seguintes áreas:

Maiores índices acumulados na Rede Telemétrica do Alto Tietê

76,6mm Córrego Sapateiro - Parque Ibirapuera

56,6mm Córrego Zavuvus - Praça Tuney arantes

54,0mm Ribeirão dos Meninos - Clube são Jose/São Paulo

30,4mm Córrego Pirajuçara - Jardim Maria Sampaio

Em cerca de 1h30, o temporal com chuva mais intensa, granizo e ventos fortes deixou um rastro de destruição, caos e morte na cidade de São Paulo na quarta-feira (14). Uma mulher de 47 anos morreu soterrada após a casa onde estava deslizar de uma encosta , na Zona Norte. O temporal também alagou ruas e o túnel do Anhangabaú, no Centro, deixou carros e ônibus submersos, derrubou árvores e provocou transtornos no transporte público e aéreo.

Vídeos gravados por testemunhas mostram veículos debaixo d'água no túnel do Anhangabaú e na Avenida 23 de Maio, além de uma mulher sendo arrastada pela enxurrada na Zona Norte. Ela foi salva por outra pessoa (veja vídeos e fotos nesta reportagem) .

No Centro, 26 carros e dois ônibus ficaram completamente submersos no túnel do Anhangabaú, onde quatro pessoas foram resgatadas pelos bombeiros. Segundo a Prefeitura, as seis bombas do local funcionaram, mas não deram conta de escoar toda a água. O Centro de Gerenciamento de Emergências Climáticas (CGE) registrou 42 milímetros de chuva em 40 minutos na região. Por volta das 19h15, uma faixa foi liberada.

Carros e ônibus boiam no túnel do Anhangabaú durante chuva forte em SP — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

Avenida 23 de Maio ficou alagada e carros acabaram submersos. — Foto: Reprodução/Arquivo pessoal

Na Zona Sul, carros ficaram parcialmente submersos na Avenida 23 de Maio , e o lago do Parque Ibirapuera transbordou, derrubando uma grade e alagando vias internas e pistas de caminhada. A concessionária Urbia registrou 97 milímetros de chuva no parque em menos de uma hora. O Córrego do Sapateiro, na Vila Mariana, também transbordou.

Segundo a Urbia, o sistema de drenagem funcionou normalmente, mas o grande volume de água vindo dos córregos do entorno provocou o transbordamento do lago e danificou a mureta com gradil do Portão 8. A concessionária informou que não houve feridos e que o parque reabriu normalmente às 5h desta quinta-feira (15), após trabalhos de limpeza realizados durante a madrugada. Ao todo, 120 profissionais atuam na vistoria, limpeza e recuperação das áreas afetadas.

Carros amontoados após inundação no túnel do Anhangabaú, em SP — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Segundo o CGE, a chuva mais intensa durou cerca de uma hora e meia. Em vídeo nas redes sociais, o prefeito Ricardo Nunes (MDB) afirmou que "choveu 40%, em poucos minutos, do que era pra chover o mês inteiro" . A Prefeitura informou que fará um levantamento dos prejuízos.

Residência atingida por deslizamento de terra na Brasilândia, Zona Norte de SP — Foto: Reprodução

Segundo a Secretaria da Segurança Pública (SSP), a vítima que morreu foi encontrada entre os escombros da casa que desabou por causa da chuva na Zona Norte.

Moradores a retiraram antes da chegada das equipes de resgate. O caso foi registrado no 72º Distrito Policial (DP), na Vila Penteado, e a polícia requisitou perícia. A identidade dela não foi divulgada.

No Bixiga, região central, uma pensão desabou parcialmente na Rua Conselheiro Ramalho e foi interditada pela Defesa Civil em razão do temporal. Segundo o governo estadual, não havia moradores no imóvel. Até as 19h, a Prefeitura registrava 16 ocorrências de queda de árvores, além de chamados para desabamentos e deslizamentos.

Área do Terminal Bandeira, no Centro da capital, alagada após forte chuva — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

A água invadiu acessos da estação Japão-Liberdade , da Linha 1-Azul do Metrô, além de acessos das estações Paraíso e Trianon-Masp , na Linha 2-Verde. A circulação dos trens não foi interrompida na estação Japão-Liberdade.

No Terminal Bandeira , os ônibus municipais ficaram temporariamente parados entre 16h e 17h. Na Linha 7-Rubi , os trens circularam com velocidade reduzida entre Palmeiras-Barra Funda e a cidade de Jundiaí após uma falha de sinalização provocada pela chuva, segundo a concessionária TIC Trens.

Alagamento na Av. Nove de Julho — Foto: Reprodução

O Aeroporto de Congonhas teve 24 voos cancelados — 11 chegadas e 13 partidas —, segundo a concessionária Aena. Também houve atrasos. O túnel Congonhas, próximo ao aeroporto, ficou alagado.

Entre 15h e 18h, o Corpo de Bombeiros atendeu 11 ocorrências de queda de árvores , 17 de enchentes e quatro de desabamentos. Na Bela Vista, uma árvore caiu sobre dois carros na Rua Plínio Figueiredo. Por causa dos transtornos, a Prefeitura suspendeu o rodízio municipal de veículos das 17h às 20h.

Unidades de saúde também foram afetadas. Segundo a Secretaria Estadual da Saúde, os atendimentos foram mantidos e pacientes foram remanejados sem prejuízo à assistência.

Céu de São Paulo em foto tirada na chegada da primavera, em setembro de 2026. — Foto: ALOISIO MAURICIO/FOTOARENA/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

A Defesa Civil estadual prevê novas chuvas fortes nesta quinta-feira (15). Os acumulados podem chegar a 80 milímetros na Grande São Paulo, na Baixada Santista e no Vale do Ribeira; a 70 milímetros no Litoral Norte e no Vale do Paraíba; e a volumes entre 50 e 75 milímetros nas regiões de Campinas e Sorocaba.

O governo informou que o Gabinete de Crise segue monitorando as ocorrências. A orientação é evitar áreas alagadas, não se abrigar sob árvores e acompanhar os alertas oficiais.

articles.title: Alex Murdaugh's 'wild goose chase' for missing murder guns targets police chief: expert
articles.summary: Alex Murdaugh's defense claims a Yemassee police chief was seen with the murder weapons, but a former prosecutor calls it a "wild goose chase."
articles.body: LEXINGTON, S.C. — A former prosecutor said Alex Murdaugh’s defense team is pursuing a "wild goose chase" over claims a police chief handled the alleged murder weapons as the case returns to court Friday. Murdaugh was convicted in 2023 of murdering his wife, Maggie, and son, Paul, at the family's Moselle property in Colleton County. A hearing is scheduled for Friday morning at 10 a.m. to discuss several evidentiary items as both the prosecution and Murdaugh's defense prepare for a retrial next year. The South Carolina Supreme Court later overturned the convictions after finding that former Colleton County Clerk of Court Becky Hill improperly influenced the jury. His retrial is scheduled to begin April 5, 2027. Murdaugh has maintained his innocence in the killings. ALEX MURDAUGH MURDER SAGA LANDS RIGHT BACK WHERE IT STARTED BEFORE NEXT LOWCOUNTRY COURTROOM BATTLE At the center of Friday's hearing are several motions relating to DNA evidence tied to Maggie Murdaugh's fingernail clippings and her cellphone swabs, ballistics evidence, raw data from the cellphones seized during the investigation, and raw crime scene data that includes the FARO laser scan of the crime scene. A separate hearing will be held on Nov. 13, where more motions will be heard. The defense team for Murdaugh had previously sought the release of DNA evidence collected from beneath Maggie Murdaugh's fingernails to Othram, Inc. for analysis. Following Othram's testing, the defense contended that further analysis is necessary to recover a male DNA profile that, according to the defense, the state crime lab identified but did not fully investigate. ALEX MURDAUGH DEFENSE POINTS TO UNKNOWN MALE DNA IN PUSH FOR NEW TESTING Murdaugh defense attorney Dick Harpootlian argued that the partial DNA profile from swabs on Maggie Murdaugh's phone should be further tested as well. Defense attorneys asked for a list of every shooting in the counties surrounding the crime scene where .300 Blackout cases or projectiles were recovered, along with details about each crime. They also asked for raw data from a 3D laser scan the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division (SLED) took of the crime scene. Prosecutors handed over a read-only viewer file in 2022, but the defense says it needs the raw data to reconstruct the scene. MURDAUGH DEFENSE SAYS DETECTIVES FOUND MALE DNA UNDER VICTIM'S NAILS BUT SKIPPED KEY TESTING In a recent filing, prosecutors said "the state is happy to provide" the original scans of the crime scene done by a laser reconstruction device. Prosecutors also called Murdaugh's ballistics request a "speculative fishing expedition for public consumption." The state also said the phone data they requested was produced to them in 2022, and accused Murdaugh's defense of spreading "brazen falsehoods" in its motion. Murdaugh's defense team also asked a judge to force prosecutors to turn over information it has "concerning the handling, transport, concealment, or disposal of the alleged weapons used to kill Maggie Murdaugh and Paul Murdaugh, including the statement a witness gave to agents of the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division in 2023 that a Lowcountry police chief spoke of arriving early at the scene and of providing Defendant Murdaugh a change of clothes, the reports of every interview conducted on that subject, and the testimony and exhibits presented to the State Grand Jury concerning it." MURDAUGH LAWYERS ALLEGE PROSECUTORS WITHHELD WITNESS CLAIM THAT POLICE CHIEF HANDLED MURDER WEAPONS: FILING According to the motion, filed in late September by Murdaugh's attorneys, press reports indicate that a state grand jury received testimony alleging Yemassee Police Chief Greg Alexander was observed in possession of the murder weapons shortly after the June 7, 2021, killings. "According to those reports, witnesses have testified that the Chief of Police of the Town of Yemassee, Greg Alexander, was seen with the murder weapons in the immediate aftermath of the June 7, 2021, killings, and that second Yemassee officer is under investigation for transporting and concealing weapons and clothing," the filing states. ALEX MURDAUGH DEMANDS NEW EVIDENCE SEARCH IN HUNT FOR CRACKS IN CASE It cites a story from The Post and Courier, which reported that "a Lowcountry official told SLED agents that Chief Alexander 'spoke of arriving early to the murder scene and talked about providing a change of clothes to Murdaugh,' and that the official believed the guns and clothing were brought into the police station and stored there." Notably, the allegations couldn't be corroborated by The Post and Courier. ALEX MURDAUGH DEFENSE SAYS MURDER WEAPON MAY BE TIED TO SEPARATE KILLING AS JUDGE SEEKS ANSWERS During Murdaugh's first murder trial in 2023, prosecutors argued that he used two different types of weapons to kill his family members, then cleaned up with a nearby water hose, changed his clothes and drove to his parents' house, where he allegedly left the murder weapons. He purportedly returned a week later to dispose of them. Prosecutors had previously acknowledged that the weapons were never recovered by police. According to an Oct. 8 filing by prosecutors, they neither confirmed nor denied that the matter might be under investigation but said that grand jury proceedings are confidential. Prosecutors said they will turn over the information when legally obligated. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X Alexander, through his attorney, Joe McCulloch, denied accusations made in the media reports. "The same explanation has been provided to SLED," McCulloch told Fox News Digital. "That truth will outlive any ridiculous rumors and gossip." ALEX MURDAUGH MAKES 'EXPLOSIVE' BID TO BLOW UP MURDER CASE HINGING ON DNA, DIRTY MONEY AND LIES: EXPERT His attorneys said "if the reports are accurate," prosecutors have held evidence that contradicts their own theory. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS Former prosecutor Joshua Ritter told Fox News Digital he considers the allegation against Alexander a "wild goose chase." CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB "This is one of those cases that, you know, a lot of reporting was done early on, a lot of conspiracy theories swirling around this case," Ritter said. "I don't see any reason for the judge to allow for this essentially wild goose chase in regards to an uncorroborated report about law enforcement perhaps being in possession of the murder weapon." SEND US A TIP "Obviously, the defense would love to pursue this to its absolute limit because they think that there's a snowball's chance that it might yield something, but I think that the judge is probably going to give very little leeway on something like this," he added. To be fair, I think from their perspective, they would say we're allowed to zealously defend our client. And if part of that means that we have access to every piece of evidence, including the raw data, so that we can do our own independent testing of it, no one should judge us for that," he said. "And that's very true, but at the same time, this is not the first time they've seen this evidence. This is not the first time they've had a trial regarding this evidence, this is our second go around." articles.title: Salma Hayek’s billionaire husband backed Notre-Dame with a €100 million pledge after the 2019 fire; restoration efforts brought the 860 year old historic Paris landmark back in 2024
articles.summary: In April 2019, a fire tore through Paris’s Notre-Dame Cathedral, destroying its roof and bringing down its famous spire.
articles.body: In April 2019, a fire tore through Paris’s Notre-Dame Cathedral, destroying its roof and bringing down its famous spire. The damage threatened parts of a landmark whose history stretches back more than 860 years. Among those who stepped forward to help fund its restoration were French billionaire François-Henri Pinault and his father, François Pinault, who pledged €100 million through their family holding company, according to the New York Post. Actor Salma Hayek’s husband Pinault, joined other major donors in supporting the rebuilding effort. More than five years later, Notre-Dame reopened in December 2024, welcoming visitors back to its restored interior.Notre-Dame Cathedral fire in 2019 caused extensive damage to the historic landmarkAccording to Friends of Notre-Dame de Paris, the fire broke out on 15 April 2019, sending flames and thick smoke above the Île de la Cité, the historic island in the River Seine where Notre-Dame is located. As emergency crews fought to contain the blaze, part of the cathedral’s roof collapsed and its central spire fell. Images of the burning structure travelled around the world, prompting concern over the survival of one of France’s most recognisable historic buildings.Although the fire destroyed much of the timber roof structure and damaged parts of the cathedral, the main stone structure remained standing. The towers and many of the building’s principal features survived, along with important artworks and religious objects that firefighters and emergency teams helped protect.Notre-Dame had undergone centuries of alterations and repairs, and restoring it would require a careful assessment of the surviving structure before reconstruction could begin. The immediate challenge was to stabilise the building, protect it from further deterioration and determine how its damaged sections could be rebuilt.How Salma Hayek’s billionaire husband supported Notre-Dame’s restorationThe pledge placed the Pinault family among the prominent private donors responding to the disaster. François-Henri Pinault, who is married to Hayek, leads Kering, the luxury group associated with luxurious brands. His father founded the business that eventually developed into the group and built a substantial fortune through investments in luxury goods and other sectors.“My father François Pinault and myself have decided to release a sum of €100 million from our Artemis funds, the family holding company, to participate in the effort that will be necessary for the complete reconstruction of Notre-Dame.”The family’s contribution was widely reported in the aftermath of the fire, as wealthy individuals and companies offered financial support for the rebuilding campaign. The donation was intended to help meet the cost of restoring the cathedral, rather than fund a separate project bearing the family’s name.The Arnault family, associated with luxury conglomerate LVMH, and the Bettencourt Meyers family also announced major contributions.How Notre-Dame was rebuilt after the devastating 2019 fireThe reconstruction was not simply a matter of replacing the sections destroyed by the fire. Specialists had to secure the building, remove damaged materials and develop a plan that respected Notre-Dame’s historic fabric. The work involved traditional craftsmanship alongside modern engineering and conservation techniques.Restoring the roof and rebuilding the spire were among the most visible parts of the project. As reported by Friends of Notre-Dame de Paris, the spire, originally designed by architect Eugène Viollet-le-Duc during the 19th century, had become a defining feature of the Paris skyline. Its reconstruction followed the historic design, returning a familiar silhouette to the cathedral.Inside, teams worked on the stonework, vaults, decorative elements and other features affected by the fire, smoke and the subsequent emergency operations. Cleaning and conservation were also necessary to bring the interior back into use.As reported by the BBC, French President Emmanuel Macron had expressed, “We'll rebuild Notre-Dame even more beautifully and I want it to be completed in five years, we can do it.” The cathedral ultimately reopened in December 2024, just over five years and seven months after the fire.Notre-Dame welcomed visitors again in December 2024Reportedly, the reopening ceremonies took place on 7 and 8 December 2024, bringing together political leaders, religious figures, public officials and invited guests. Hayek and Pinault attended the ceremony on 7 December, when the restored cathedral became the focus of international attention once again.More than 1,500 guests were reported to have attended the event, including world leaders and other prominent figures. The gathering marked a significant moment for Paris, where Notre-Dame has long served as a place of worship and a destination for visitors interested in French history and architecture.The reopening also allowed people to see the results of years of painstaking restoration. The cathedral’s interior had been cleaned and repaired, while the rebuilt roof and spire restored much of its familiar appearance. The work aimed to preserve the character of the historic building while making it possible to continue using it safely.A historic landmark restored for future generationsReportedly, Notre-Dame’s origins date to the 12th century, when construction began under Bishop Maurice de Sully. Building work started around 1163, and the cathedral developed over the following centuries, with major additions and changes shaping the structure seen today. Its long history includes periods of religious and political upheaval, restoration and changing uses.The building is associated with major events in French history and has inspired generations of artists and writers. Victor Hugo’s 1831 novel The Hunchback of Notre-Dame helped bring renewed public attention to the cathedral during the 19th century, when its condition had deteriorated and restoration was becoming a pressing concern.You use AI every day. articles.title: Malibu brush fire grows to 200 acres, prompts evacuation orders and warnings
articles.summary: Evacuation orders and warnings are in place as crews battle a fast-moving brush fire in far western Malibu amid hot and windy conditions, officials said.
articles.body: Evacuation orders and warnings are in place as crews battle a fast-moving brush fire in far western Malibu amid hot and windy conditions on Thursday, officials said. The Bryson Fire was reported near Mulholland Highway and Encinal Canyon Road in rugged terrain in the Santa Monica Mountains near the Ventura County line just before 5 p.m., according to the Los Angeles County Fire Department. It grew to 200 acres and was 0% contained as of Thursday night. Authorities issued an evacuation order for the Encinal Canyon area near Trancas Canyon. Other surrounding areas, including Zuma Beach, were under evacuation warnings. The latest evacuation information is available on the Genasys Protect website. The Red Cross opened an emergency shelter at Agoura High School, located at 8545 West Driver Avenue. “There’s not really much you can do except, you know, wait and hope that, you know, all these wonderful firemen will get control of it,” said evacuee Susan Booker, who previously lost her home to the Woolsey Fire in 2018. “But it’s really windy, and it’s really scary to see this happening again so close to the house.” The Los Angeles County Probation Department said 38 youth from Campus Vernon Kilpatrick were evacuated to Barry J. Nidorf Juvenile Hall/SYTF in Sylmar. The Bryson Fire was burning around 8 miles from Pepperdine University. The school said in a social media post that the fire did not threaten its Malibu campus and that winds were blowing away from the campus. Officials said no structures have been lost and no injuries have been reported. The firefight comes as a red flag warning is expected to remain in effect for most valleys and coasts of Los Angeles and Ventura counties until 8 p.m. Saturday. LA County Fire Public Information Officer Keith Navarre described Thursday’s conditions as “vulnerable,” pointing to the dry air and strong winds. “It makes it hard, and it makes the fire move faster through the dry fuel,” Navarre said. Gusts in the area were between 20 and 30 miles per hour around 7:15 p.m., according to NBC4 Meteorologist Shanna Mendiola, who said she expected winds to weaken and temperatures to drop in the hours after sunset before picking back up after sunrise Friday. “We’re working hard to keep it contained and stop it generally while it gets dark and the winds kind of die down a little bit,” Navarre said. Navarre recommended people to charge their cellphones and keep their gas tanks full in case of planned power outages or downed power lines from high winds. LA County Fire said its resources for the Bryson Fire include more than 300 personnel, two Super Scoopers and multiple firefighting aircraft that can operate at night. It’s unclear what started the fire.

articles.title: Councils warned of risks of high street pedestrianisation
articles.summary: The government says the process "needs to be well considered", warning that banning traffic could damage local economies.
articles.body:
The UK government has warned councils against ill-considered plans to pedestrianise high streets in England.

In evidence submitted to an inquiry by MPs, the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) said pedestrianisation can make high streets "more attractive, safe and welcoming".

But the department added that "the process needs to be well considered", warning that removing traffic could make high streets less accessible and damage local economies.

"Local leaders pursuing pedestrianisation must be aware of the risks and work to mitigate them, within a broader spatial strategy," the evidence says.

The evidence was submitted to the Housing, Communities and Local Government Committee, which is investigating the action needed to revitalise England's high streets.

An MHCLG spokesperson said the government had not issued formal guidance to local authorities on pedestrianisation.

The government is due to publish a new strategy on high streets later this year.

"We support local leaders to make their own choices about pedestrianisation based on the needs of their communities," the spokesperson said.

"Our upcoming high streets strategy will also set out more detail on how we are bringing high streets back to life and making sure they are accessible for everyone."

Studies suggest banning cars from high streets has become increasingly common in city and town centres across the UK.

Some councils attempted pedestrianisation experiments during the Covid pandemic, which spurred debates about the use of outdoor public spaces.

But the pedestrianisation of some high streets has proved contentious, particularly in London, London Mayor Sadiq Khan has clashed with the local council over plans to make Oxford Street traffic-free .

Parts of Oxford Street will be pedestrianised from 26 October.

The London mayor's spokesperson said he was focused on making high streets "cleaner, greener and more pleasant places to spend time, and helping to drive economic growth and prosperity".

"Pedestrianisation can help reduce conflict between vehicles and pedestrians, making high streets more attractive for visitors and shoppers," the mayor's spokesperson said.

They added the Greater London Authority would use data and feedback from the Oxford Street scheme to "understand how a range of people will use the newly pedestrianised space, and help refine the design of permanent improvements".

Most pedestrianisation schemes are immediately countered by some level of local opposition, said Professor Lee Ivett, who heads the School of Architecture at the University of the Built Environment.

He told the BBC that while opposition usually focuses on short-term disruption to local businesses, evidence does suggest that pedestrianisation increases the economic viability of high streets in the long run.

But he said pedestrianisation had to be paired with improvements in public transport to realise those economic benefits.

"If you want to defeat the argument that a reduction in the amount of traffic will reduce the amount of trade, then you need to also be able to make an argument that an investment in public transport infrastructure is actually going to be the vehicle that still keeps providing accessibility to the centre," Professor Ivett said.

In urban design guidance and previous high street strategies, the UK government has supported making high streets more attractive and people-friendly.

The last high street strategy - which was published in 2021 when the Conservatives were in power - said the government wanted to see more town and city centres "designed with a sense of place and to be attractive to people walking, cycling and using public transport".

But the government's approach to date has focused on giving local authorities the tools and flexibility to make their own decisions on pedestrianisation.

Pedestrianising roads can be a long and complicated legal process, involving consultations with residents and impact assessments.

It has taken a decade for London Mayor Sadiq Khan's proposal to pedestrianise parts of Oxford Street to come to fruition, after he first suggested it in 2016.

Elsewhere some pedestrianisation trials have failed. Last month, West Berkshire Council ended Newbury's evening pedestrianisation trial , after it was opposed by 75% of respondents to a public consultation.

In contrast, the majority of Stevenson Square in Manchester's Northern Quarter has transitioned into a permanent pedestrian-friendly space, following a successful trial.

articles.title: Norway wealth fund urged to ease nuclear arms ban after Gaza investment row
articles.summary: The review called for Norway’s sovereign wealth fund to lift ethical risk limitations on its investments.
articles.body:
A government-appointed committee has called for Norway’s sovereign wealth fund to lift limitations on its investments based on ethical risks, including those regarding nuclear weapons and Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

In a report released on Thursday, the committee said the world’s largest sovereign wealth fund, which controls assets totalling nearly $2.3 trillion, should be allowed to invest in companies that produce nuclear weapons. With reference to Gaza, it also called for the fund to refrain from involvement in “diplomatic” issues.

Led by former Central Bank Governor Svein Gjedrem, the committee recommended easing the fund’s investment conditions as part of a broader overhaul that would give its manager, the Central Bank, greater discretion over how it addresses ethical risks.

The review was prompted in part by controversy over the fund’s disinvestment last year from United States construction giant Caterpillar. The fund said the move was prompted by Caterpillar’s purported involvement in rights violations perpetrated by Israel amid its genocidal war on Gaza and in the occupied West Bank. Washington has since pressured Oslo over the move.

“Parts of the rationale for the appointment of the Committee was the Fund’s management related to the war in Gaza,” the committee commissioned by the government said. In the report, it argued that decisions regarding “another state’s conduct” should not be made by the fund but “reserved for the ordinary diplomatic channels of the Norwegian authorities”.

The unanimous recommendations of the committee in the report, which was submitted to the Ministry of Finance, also called for a review of the fund’s exclusion of investment in companies involved in the production of nuclear weapons.

Citing Norway’s reliance on NATO’s nuclear deterrent and a worsening security environment, the report suggested that investments in companies based in the US, United Kingdom and France that are involved in the production of nuclear weapons should be allowed.

The proposals also extended to reshaping the role of the fund’s independent ethics watchdog, allowing a number of assessments of potential investments to remain confidential.

The report has already provoked a backlash in Norway, with opposition politicians slamming the potential changes. Meanwhile, analysts suggested that weakening ethics considerations could have a wide impact.

“If the Norwegian sovereign wealth fund – often considered a global gold standard – changes its posture towards nuclear weapons, it will open Pandora’s box for many global investors to follow suit,” Lawrence Loh, director of the Centre for Governance and Sustainability at the National University of Singapore Business School, told Al Jazeera.

The committee framed the proposed change as an obligation to protect Norway’s national security, citing the country’s dependence on its allies’ nuclear umbrella.

“The global security situation has changed. Norway is building up its defence capabilities, and the protection provided by NATO’s nuclear umbrella has become increasingly important. The companies that would be reincluded produce weapons that Norway needs for its own defence”, the report argued.

Gareth Evans, former Australian foreign minister, told Al Jazeera the report was “an encouraging initiative in a world that has become alarmingly complacent about the risks of nuclear war, with every major nuclear arms control agreement dead, dying or on life support, and the longstanding taboo against threat or use eroding”.

Amid US President Donald Trump’s shake-up of NATO, European countries are increasingly looking to join France’s nuclear deterrent umbrella .

Trump said on Thursday that Washington is holding talks with Russia and China aimed at denuclearising the countries with the biggest stockpiles of nuclear weapons.

However, Loh warned that shifting the Norwegian fund’s investment conditions could encourage investment by others in nuclear companies “in scenarios different from the Norwegians’ condition of the invested companies being based in allied, nuclear-armed NATO countries”.

articles.title: Americans say they're broke. So why can't they stop spending so much?
articles.summary: Consumer confidence is in the basement, yet consumer spending keeps rising. A financial expert reveals five essential reasons behind the disconnect.
articles.body: Some Americans are crying poverty with a $1,500 iPhone in one hand and an $8 Starbucks latte in the other. They say groceries are unaffordable, but somehow the restaurants are packed, airports are crowded, and the neighbor just pulled into his driveway with a brand-new $90,000 SUV. Apparently, we're one bad economic report away from bankruptcy and one Instagram post away from booking another trip to Cabo. Consumer confidence is in the basement. Consumer spending apparently didn't get the memo. US ECONOMY NOTCHES REMARKABLE NEW RECORD, SPARKING CHEERS: ‘GOOD JOB EVERYONE’ In September, the Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index fell to 81.9. Yet it has been reported that consumer credit and debit card spending per household increased 6.2% from a year earlier. So, what's going on? IT’S NOT THE ECONOMY, STUPID. AMERICANS VOTE BASED ON THEIR PERSONAL ECONOMY As a financial advisor, I think the answer involves something more powerful than inflation or interest rates. Human psychology. And there are five reasons our spending habits aren't matching our economic anxiety. WE ALL ARE DESPERATE FOR A FINANCIAL CHECK-UP. TIME TO SAY, ‘SHOW ME THE MONEY!’ 1. Keeping up with the Joneses has gone digital Thirty years ago, you compared your lifestyle with the neighbor who bought a new Cadillac. Today, you're comparing yourself with 5,000 people on Instagram. There are even college degrees on how to become a social media influencer. None of them get lots of likes by telling you to eat ramen noodles and skip third-row seats for the latest rock concert. Someone's vacationing in Italy. Someone remodeled their kitchen. Someone bought a new Porsche. Face it. Someone is always doing better than you are. Or, it seems that way. You're comparing your everyday financial reality with everybody else's highlight reel. Social media has turned keeping up with the Joneses into keeping up with the Kardashians. Except the Kardashians can actually afford it. 3 BIG QUESTIONS TO ASK MOM AND DAD BEFORE YOU MAKE A MAJOR FINANCIAL COMMITMENT 2. We've become a nation of monthly payments Remember when people saved money before buying something? It’s called layaway. Today, almost anything can be financed. SKIP TWO YEARS OF COLLEGE DEBT AND GIVE YOUR FAMILY A LIFETIME OF WEALTH That $1,200 purchase? Just four easy payments of $300. The vacation? Monthly installments. The furniture? Zero down. Apparently, we're one bad economic report away from bankruptcy and one Instagram post away from booking another trip to Cabo. We've become experts at making expensive things look cheap by dividing them into smaller payments. GEN Z IS WORKING HARD, BUT THE ECONOMY IS PUTTING THE AMERICAN DREAM OUT OF REACH FOR MANY The problem isn't necessarily buy now, pay later. It's forgetting how many things you've already agreed to pay for later. And eventually, later shows up. 3. There are two different American consumers Not everybody spending money is financially struggling. Higher-income Americans with substantial investment portfolios have benefited from rising asset prices. Many can comfortably afford expensive vacations and new cars. Meanwhile, other households are stretching their paychecks just to maintain their lifestyles. Some spending growth also reflects higher prices for necessities. The economy isn't treating every consumer equally. When you see your neighbor's new Mercedes, you don't know whether he paid cash or financed it for 84 months. You see the car. Not the car payment. 4. If tomorrow looks bad, why not enjoy today? When people worry about the future, they don't always save more. Sometimes they spend more. Had a terrible week? Amazon makes it your birthday every day. Stressed about work? Book a vacation. Worried about the economy? Just get a good meal out at a local restaurant. Retail therapy is a lot more fun than retirement planning. Unfortunately, the happiness from that purchase may disappear long before the credit card bill does. 5. We've confused looking wealthy with being wealthy Americans have become obsessed with displaying wealth rather than accumulating it. The luxury car. The designer handbag. The vacation pictures. But here's something I've learned after decades of advising families. Net worth doesn't have an Instagram account. I've met millionaires who drive 10-year-old cars and people earning $250,000 who couldn't cover a $10,000 emergency. Income isn't wealth. And spending certainly isn't wealth. You're comparing your everyday financial reality with everybody else's highlight reel. Social media has turned keeping up with the Joneses into keeping up with the Kardashians. Start a 21-day budget cleanse Why? Because I wrote the book. So, before you swear off Starbucks forever, try three simple changes. First, put every nonessential purchase over $100 on a 48-hour waiting list or online cart. If you still want it two days later and can afford it, buy it. Third, automatically move 5% of every paycheck into savings before you spend a dime. Start smaller if your budget can't handle 5%. The point is to pay yourself before you pay everybody else. Not the other way around. This isn't about living like a monk. It's about remembering who's in charge of your money. The real consumer confidence problem I'm not suggesting Americans should stop enjoying their money. Life is meant to be lived. But there's a difference between enjoying your money and spending it to impress people who aren't paying your bills. articles.title: As a Cuban survivor, I know there is no dignity with socialism. But we all pay the price
articles.summary: Democrat Mayor Zohran Mamdani says socialism means dignity, but a Cuban-born critic and a CEA report warn DSA policies could cost much, much more.
articles.body: In a recent interview, Democrat Mayor Zohran Mamdani said: "Socialism to me, it means that you will have whatever you need to live a dignified life, and that it is the government’s job to deliver on that." If socialism gives people dignity, the Cuban people should be swimming in it. Instead, they are swimming in misery, shortages and human-rights violations. I was born in Cuba and lived 16 years of socialism. I know the difference between a political promise and what happens when government takes greater control over people's economic lives. That is why the new White House Council of Economic Advisers (CEA) report on the price tag of the Democratic Socialists of America’s policies deserves attention. SHOCKING PERCENTAGE OF DEMOCRATS IDENTIFY AS 'DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' ACCORDING TO NEW POLL: 'TOXIC POLICIES' The CEA estimates that seven major DSA proposals would cost more than $49 trillion over the next decade — roughly $355,000 per American household. Medicare for All accounts for approximately $47.4 trillion of that projected fiscal burden. The proposals also include student debt cancellation and free college, a 32-hour workweek, Green New Deal policies and rent control. Those numbers are enormous, but the debate should not stop at the price tag. It should also address how these proposals would be funded, including where the government would obtain the trillions of dollars needed to finance them and how that funding would affect taxpayers and the broader economy. 'CASTRO'S PLAYBOOK': EX-AG WARNS DOZENS OF CONGRESSIONAL BILLS ARE PUSHING SOCIALIST IDEAS These policies raise a larger question about government's role in Americans' lives. Who controls access to healthcare under Medicare for All? Who determines wages and working hours? Who controls housing prices? And what happens when more of the resources people depend on become dependent on government decisions? The DSA movement promotes expansive government programs as solutions to problems that are real: expensive healthcare, housing costs and economic insecurity. Those problems deserve serious attention. But a policy does not become effective simply because its goal is compassionate. OUR CLOSING ARGUMENT: THE MIDTERMS ARE A REFERENDUM ON WHO RUNS YOUR LIFE The word often used to justify these policies is dignity. But if the government can give you dignity, the government can also take it away. For instance, when it comes to licensing, the more difficult it is for a person to obtain a license, the harder it becomes for their small business to get off the ground. AMERICA’S QUIET SOCIALIST TAKEOVER IS SPREADING FROM TOWN HALLS TO CLASSROOMS Dignity should never be placed in the hands of government. It is an individual right. Economic independence — the ability to work, earn, save, build, own and make decisions for yourself and your family — is an important part of that dignity. There are alternatives that address these same problems while leaving more decisions with individuals. That means smaller, more accountable government; lower and simpler taxes; fewer regulations that make it harder to work, build or invest; and a free market in which businesses compete and consumers have choices. SEN TOM COTTON: DEMOCRATS SAY SOCIALISM WILL HELP. HISTORY SAYS IT WILL HURT Preserving a democratic system matters, too. Americans should remain free to disagree, organize, speak, vote and advocate for different solutions. A free society does not require everyone to reach the same conclusions; it requires freedom to make those decisions peacefully. Socialism steals freedom away. The DSA movement promotes expansive government programs as solutions to problems that are real: expensive healthcare, housing costs and economic insecurity. Those problems deserve serious attention. But a policy does not become effective simply because its goal is compassionate. America does not have to implement a failed system to prove it will fail again. We do not need to gamble away our freedoms to prove we can improve our system. I ESCAPED COMMUNISM. AMERICA MUST NOT IGNORE THE URGENT WARNING SIGNS The $49 trillion estimate should prompt more than an argument over a number. It should force Americans to examine whether expanding government control actually gives people more control over their lives — or less. Compassion matters. Affordability matters. Economic opportunity matters. So does freedom. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Because dignity is not something government can manufacture.
